checks.how: track a fixed point on the foreground figure from feet-off around 4.1s through apex to touchdown around 6.3s and fit vertical position versus time, converting pixels to metres against the large backpack unit height measured face-on in a nearby standing frame
checks.what: downward acceleration of the foreground figure during the airborne phase of the hop
checks.why: a body with nothing holding it up must accelerate downward at the local g, so the fitted acceleration directly tests the claimed world and playback speed

checks.compare_with: adult human stature norms and published spacesuit backpack dimensions
checks.how: measure the standing suited figure's full height and backpack-unit height in pixels in a standing frame around 0.0-2.1s or 6.3s and compare absolute sizes and their ratio
checks.what: standing height of the suited figure and backpack-unit size and ratio
checks.why: checks the pixel scale against independent body and hardware norms so a miniature set or costume cannot bias the gravity result

claim: Two figures in bulky white suits with backpacks move on a grey plain under a black sky presented as the lunar surface, with the foreground figure making a low two-footed hop
not_realistic_if: Not realistic if the fitted acceleration clearly misses lunar gravity or the measured sizes and hop duration clearly contradict human and equipment norms.
question: Does the foreground figure's hop fall as it would in lunar gravity?
realistic_if: Realistic if the hop's fitted downward acceleration matches lunar gravity within uncertainty and body and hardware sizes match human and equipment norms.
